body:
VS0's region analyzer (domain 2) has a real, confirmed gap: it does NOT catch a &local (address of a stack-allocated local) escaping into a returned value. Concretely: (Alt &branches) where branches is a stack-local Vec, returned as part of a PatternNode payload from parse-alt, compiled cleanly under parena build AND gcc -Wall -Wextra -pedantic with zero warnings -- but is a genuine dangling-pointer bug, only caught by actually running the generated binary under ASan (stack-use-after-return in vec_len, reading through the dangling pointer after parse-alt's own stack frame was gone). This is exactly the class of bug VS0's whole region-rank escape-checking system (Region(Source) >= Region(Destination)) is supposed to exist to catch at compile time, per NORTHSTAR.md's own core pitch -- so this is a real hole in the actual, current implementation, not a theoretical edge case. Worked around in the one real call site found (stdlib/regex/syntax.prn, PARENA commit 4b1e7fc) by passing the Vec BY VALUE instead of by reference, letting the existing non-pointer-payload auto-boxing copy it into real arena memory -- but the underlying region-analyzer gap itself is unfixed. Worth a real audit: how many OTHER places in the ~57-package stdlib take a  and hand it somewhere it could outlive the local's own stack frame? Given how young the region analyzer is (VS0 domain 2, single-pass scope tracker), this is plausibly not the only instance.

source: emily claire (CLI)
log: EMILY/claire-log.md
